question: Hrnčiar na jarmoku pred točením na kruhu dlho prehnetáva hlinu, podobne ako gazdiná cesto. Čoho sa ňou hlavne zbavuje?
source_excerpt: pri zhutňovaní hmoty treba dbať na to, aby v nej neostali vzduchové bubliny

extra.why_interesting: Watching a potter knead clay, players assume it only makes the clay softer. The real reason is hidden air bubbles, which can make a pot burst in the kiln. A player can work this out from experience with dough.
extra.verification_notes: Wedging/kneading clay before throwing is mainly done to expel air bubbles (also homogenizes); no contradicting or newer information found, though I found no Slovak source stating it directly.

explanation: Bublinka uväznená v hline sa pri vypaľovaní v peci rozpína. Hrnček potom môže prasknúť alebo doslova vybuchnúť a poškodiť aj ostatné nádoby v peci.

question: V starých kováčskych dielňach bývalo zámerne šero a kováč na jarmoku si rád postaví vyhňu do tieňa. Prečo mu ostré slnko prekáža pri práci so železom?
alternative_answers: Aby rozoznal, ako je železo rozpálené
source_excerpt: bright light masks the heat color with the surface color

extra.why_interesting: Players assume a dark smithy is just old-fashioned, or that the smith is avoiding heat. The real reason is that the colour of the glowing iron is the smith's thermometer, and sunlight washes it out. Anyone who has seen a glowing coal in daylight can reason their way there.
extra.verification_notes: Blacksmiths judge heat by glow colour, and bright light masks it, so they work in shade (https://anvilfire.com/21st-century-blacksmithing/colors-of-the-forge); the answer is a slightly loose paraphrase but defensible.

explanation: Teplotu železa kováč odhaduje podľa farby žiary, od tmavočervenej po žltobielu. Na slnku tieto odtiene zbledne, takže by železo ľahko prepálil alebo by kul príliš studené.
